en: H-hey, what happened...?! Old\nman! Everyone!
Dammit... I can't believe Raza's\nship found us... I thought the\nbribes had settled everything...
I've finally found you, Mr. Heath\nBureau.
...What... did you say?
I never imagined you'd be\ntaken in by the pirates of\nStardust Bazaar.

While it's helpful that they take
in refugees, it's problematic
that they force children into
illegal work.
...Who the hell are you...?

I am Lieutenant Jeanne
Marswest of the Raza Space
Force. Your parents have filed
a missing persons report for
you.
...He... Heath!
Mmph... Ah, sorry, I must've\ndozed off for a second.
...You were having a nightmare.
Just a dream about the old\ndays. What, were you worried\nabout me?
...Your sleep-talking was\ngrating.
Sorry about that. So, since you\nwoke me up, does that mean\nwe've arrived?
...Yes. You promised to work.
Yeah, yeah. Hmm... so, who's\nheading down?
Euwin, Welch, and Karlyn.
Who's the target and where?
Smugglers from Ober. On\n<font color=yellow>Rigas, a moon of Planet Incar</font>.
Got it. Well then, let's get to\nwork!
...Heath, just so you know...

I know. I was part of the family
until four years ago. My
weapon is still the same one
from back then.
...Then it's fine.
All right, I'm heading out.

Another place that's nothing
but a lonely sight. It definitely
feels like the perfect spot for
a black market deal!

When I looked down from the
sky, I saw the ruins of a city in
the distance. It looked like it
used to be prosperous, so I
wonder why there's no one
here.
Well, there's a reason for that.\nSorry about this, but the rules\nfor these deals are a pain.
It's okay. I'm used to it; this\nhappens all the time.
Happens all the time? We've\nbeen walked all over the place\nfor no reason!

Besides, aren't we wide open
here? What if someone shoots
us from those ruins and just
steals the goods?

That's a standard tactic in
black market deals. It's to stay
alert for authorities tailing you
or ambushes. Sometimes they'll
strike from a distance.
What!? Strike? You mean\nattack us? Why on earth would\nthey do that!

They might hold back a little,
but it's a way of deciding that
they won't deal with any idiot
who messes up here.

Wow. It feels kind of weird that
Eu's experience traveling
Rubarika is actually useful in
space.
Maybe it just means that\npeople never really change.
Now then, it looks like that's\nenough chatting.
Right on time.
It's not Thornite, is it?
Don't worry. It looks like...
It's definitely our contact!!
They won't ambush us, but\nthey should be pretty tough.\nStay sharp!
Smuggler: Hehe... looks like the\nRose family still keeps some\nimpeccable skill on their side.
...It's nothing special.
Smuggler: Don't be so modest.

Smuggler: Since the cargo was
smaller than I expected, I
worried that Gartoga was
finally on the decline, but it
seems I was mistaken.

Smuggler: I haven't seen Gems
of this purity in years. How on
earth did you get your hands
on these?
...Trade secret.
Smuggler: Figures. I'd like to\nkeep things on good terms with\nyou people.

Fighting creatures and
machines sent by the traders
at every waypoint, and only
starting the trade upon
victory...

...Why use such an inefficient
method? It feels as though
both parties only suffer
losses...

That's just how smuggling
works in wartime. You never
know where the military has
cast their nets. It was a
common practice back in
Rubarika, too.

We're in no position to defy
Lavarnia right now. Unless we
see a truly atrocious outcome,
we have no choice but to
comply.
...Coro, what do you think?
...So far, I have found no traces\nthat seem to belong to Ms.\nEve.
...I see.

Tika. Keep your spirits up. For
now, we have no choice but to
move forward one step at a
time.
Yeah... you're right.
Alright, we're back safe and\nsound!
Welcome back, Euwin! Good\nwork, everyone. How did it go?
...The smugglers here didn't\nknow anything about Thornite\neither.
And of course, nothing about\nEve...
No, they didn't recognize any\nblack monsters like the ones\nGivel was summoning, either.
...I see.
I'm not sure if this counts as a\nconsolation, but I did hear\nsomething interesting.

Apparently, over the last five
months or so, Ober has been
pushing back Raza's army in
several places.

He sounded quite pleased,
saying it's the most successful
streak since the war began.
Honestly.

How is it actually? If the tide
of battle shifted that
drastically, you'd think we'd
feel it on the front lines.

Well, the front where we and
Isabel were stationed was
focused on attacking civilian
space stations.

We weren't in a position to see
the overall war effort, and I
haven't heard of any place
taking a catastrophic loss.
Then again, it's possible the\ninformation was being\nsuppressed.

Could it be that the reports of
Ober winning are themselves
the result of information
control?
Perhaps Ober is simply saying\nthat to boost the morale of the\nmilitary and the civilians...
No, that's not it. I think Ober\nreally is winning.
...I think so too.
How can you be so sure?
No matter how much you\ncontrol information, the price\nof money and goods doesn't lie.

Even if they are smugglers,
those people are still
merchants. Business is
probably actually booming.
...I agree. ...Welch, did you used\nto be in business too?
I was a blacksmith. The price\nof metal is directly affected by\nwar.
The prices would swing up and\ndown to an almost amusing\ndegree.

It's possible they're
manipulating information by
controlling the markets
themselves.
Even so, that would mean the\neconomy has enough surplus\nto absorb those losses.
If even the low-level merchants\ncan feel a boom, I think\nsomething is really going on.
Hmm... I'm afraid I'm a bit out\nof my depth with these sorts\nof things...
I didn't know there were things\nyou weren't good at, Verda.

There are quite a few. To do
business, one must be able to
read the hearts of the people,
yes?
In that regard, I... couldn't even\ndecipher the heart of a single\ncomrade...
...Yeah. You're right... I wonder\nwhat happened to Eve...
...Judging by the situation, it\nseems your companion... Ms.\nEve, has stolen our Gems.
T-that's...

...These are precious goods
that my family spent a great
deal of time and money
collecting. At this rate, lending
you a ship is the least of our
concerns.
H-how much money are we\ntalking about?
If you think you can simply pay\nus back, you are naive.

Even if we had the money now,
we cannot replace the goods
meant for our clients. The loss
of trust cannot be measured in
money...
Y-you're right...
Practically speaking, even if we\ncaught Evelysse now, the lost\nGems wouldn't just come back.
Her summons require a price.
...You mean she already used\nthe stones?
That is the most logical\nconclusion.
Ugh... T-then what are we\nsupposed to do...
...Lover. Right now, I've been\ncast out and left alone in the\nBazaar.

I'll start from the very bottom
of the Rose family and earn
back every single Gem that
was lost. So, please, let the
Captain and the others...
Heath! You can't!

Even in the short time I've
known her, I can tell that Eve
isn't the kind of woman who
would just act lawlessly.

But since things have turned
out this way, it's my
responsibility for relying on you
and introducing you to Lover
and the others.
...How much do you think your\nown value is worth?

Even if you worked your entire
life, you wouldn't make back
half of the Gems that were just
lost.
...Wh-what is it, Captain?
Responsibility... Captain, you\ndon't mean...
...Do you possess high-purity\nGems?

You didn't even know what
Gems were in the Azurite
system, so how can you claim
that yours are of high purity?
...Fine. But you must have seen\nhow many Gems were here.
If the quality doesn't make up\nfor the lack of quantity, I won't\naccept them.
If that happens, I'll have no\nchoice but to leave the final\ndecision to my father.
I will not compromise. Be\nprepared.
We didn't have nearly enough,\nbut Lavarnia went quiet the\nmoment she saw them.
Ricardo said he would not ask\nfor details to avoid\nunnecessary interference,

but now that things have come
to this, it would be wise for us
to understand how Gems are
used in the Azurite system.

You're right. If people are
fighting wars and smuggling
them, they must be incredibly
important...
W-what?!
I'm detecting weapons. A\nstarship is engaging in combat\nat extremely close range!
What?!
Don't tell me one of the armies\nfound us?
No, there shouldn't be any\nRaza or Ober ships in this\narea.
I'm confirming this with the\ndata being sent by Rekoro.
Valka, could this be the\ntransport ship from the deal\nwe just made?

It appears so. It seems the
smuggler's transport ship fired
a physical weapon while in the
atmosphere of the satellite
Rigas.
It was only one shot, so maybe\nthey just destroyed some large\ndebris...
...Wait, what!?
S-signal lost! I've detected a\nheat source from the transport\nship exploding!
What happened? Was it taken\ndown by a long-range attack!?
N-no, that shouldn't be\npossible... For one, I don't see\nany such reaction anywhere...!
Hmm!?
What is it this time!
Well, I can't be sure since we\ncouldn't replace the Overman's\noptical sensors...

I've spotted a small fighter that
appears to have attacked the
smugglers' transport. I'll put it
on the screen.
...Is that a fighter? It blends\ninto the color of space, making\nit hard to tell.

If the other ship was shot
down, isn't there any evidence
that this fighter fired
something?
That's the thing... I couldn't\ndetect any.

I cross-referenced it with the
data sent by the AI Rekoro,
but there are only traces of
fire coming from the transport.
As for the transport in\nquestion...
Ugh... look at this...
The hull is completely snapped\nin two...
There's no way anyone\nsurvived that. It looks as if it\nwere hit by a meteorite.
Can you tell which faction that\nfighter-like thing belongs to?
First, I can't even confirm if it's\na fighter... but the shape\nseems similar to an Ober ship.
However, cross-referencing it\nwith the Overman's data shows\nno matching vessels.
...In Ober, many different races\nsend volunteers and\nmercenaries to the military.

It is impossible to keep track
of every single ship, and the
Overman only carries data that
interests me.
I would not rely on it too\nheavily.
By the way, I have another\nunpleasant report.
What else could there possibly\nbe?
About that mysterious combat\nship... it flew off in the\ndirection we are heading.
Furthermore, it moved as if it\nwere tracing the ideal course I\ncalculated.
A mere coincidence...
...is something we should\nprobably not assume.
...Right.
There's no point in just thinking\nabout it.

Heath, Lavarnia. Let's head
toward that ship to rescue
anyone on board first, then
move to the next point.
Also... there's something I want\nyou to tell me.
...What is it?
About the war between Raza\nand Ober. As much detail as\nyou can.
...Originally, Ober and Raza\nachieved space colonization at\nalmost the same time.
There are 36 planets in total in\nthe Azurite system.
The planets in the habitable\nzone are Planet Raza and\nPlanet Ober.
Next are the moon Rigas and\nthe Stardust Bazaar.
...And finally, <font color=yellow>Planet Lazuli</font>.
Of these, only Raza, Ober, and\nthe Bazaar are inhabited by\nhumans.

And the planet that the old
man from Gartoga
mentioned―the one Raza and
Ober are fighting over―is
Planet Lazuli.
<font color=blue>Lavarnia</font>: The moon Rigas was\na mining world.

It was rich in Gems throughout
the entire planet, and Raza and
Ober, who had only recently
entered space, shared these
resources peacefully.

<font color=blue>Welch</font>: But now they're fighting
over Gems, right? Why can't
they do it like they did back
then?
<font color=blue>Heath</font>: That was shortly after\nthey first entered space.

Back then, their starships were
far more primitive than they
are now. Forget warships; just
leaving their home planets was
a life-or-death gamble.

Both sides understood that it
wouldn't be wise to fight with
the humans they had just
made first contact with in the
same star system.
<font color=blue>Karlyn</font> How ironic that they\nwere peaceful simply because\nthey lacked the means to fight.

<font color=blue>Heath</font> Far from having the
means to fight, Raza was
suffering from a planetary
energy crisis at the time.

Apparently, the entire planet
was on the brink of collapse if
they couldn't get their hands
on Gems.
In a situation like that, you'd\nonly be a complete fool not to\nsecure resources peacefully.

<font color=blue>Verda</font> It is impressive that
they were able to develop
enough to expand into space
as they have now, despite such
desperation.

<font color=blue>Ricardo</font> But once Raza gained
momentum... wouldn't Ober
have found it impossible to just
stand by and watch?
<font color=blue>Lavarnia</font> Ober had its own\ninternal racial conflicts during\nthat era.

Civil war was raging across the
planet, and the success of the
space exploration project was
directly tied to the success of
establishing a unified planetary
government.

They were in no position to be
fighting with the people they
had just made first contact
with.

<font color=blue>Euwin</font> I see. Rubarika wouldn't
have had the luxury of making
other enemies during the Holy
War either.

<font color=blue>Heath</font> Yeah... anyway, back
then, both planets joined
forces and got along well
enough.
<font color=blue>Heath</font> Besides, the Gems\nmined from the moon Rigas...

...were many times more
efficient than the energy
sources Raza had been using
for space development until
then. Because of this, both
planets saw a dramatic leap in
their technology.

<font color=blue>Tika</font> So, you're saying they
started fighting because their
technology improved enough to
actually wage war?

<font color=blue>Ricardo</font> No, that's not the root
cause. You can tell just by
looking at the current state of
Rigas.
<font color=blue>Verda</font> I presume the Gem\nreserves on Rigas have run\ndry?
<font color=blue>Heath</font> Exactly. All that's left on\nRigas now are old-fashioned\nfossil fuels like coal and oil.

A society that's grown
accustomed to Gems couldn't
possibly function on such
inefficient energy.
Once the Gems were gone,\npeople abandoned this planet\nlike a receding tide.

<font color=blue>Euwin</font> So, Raza and Ober
began fighting because they
were both searching for new
Gem mining sites.
<font color=blue>Lavarnia</font> ...Though it seems\nthings didn't turn sour quite so\nsuddenly back then...

The relationship deteriorated
decisively about 100 years
ago, after a massive new vein
of Gems was discovered to
replace Rigas.
It's a place you all know well.
...No way.
The Stardust Bazaar!?
...Yes. An asteroid belt crossing\nthe habitable zone of the\nAzurite system.
Someone pioneered the\ndevelopment of that area.

Back when Gems first started
getting attention, he
established Gem research on
Rigas.
The founder of the Stardust\nBazaar was a man beloved by\nboth the Raza and the Ober.

Hmm...? You mean someone
from the earliest days of Gem
research was still around only
100 years ago?

Gem research began hundreds
of years ago, did it not? Is it
even possible for someone to
live that long?

Some Ober races are
long-lived. Though, it's not
exactly known whether he was
Raza or Ober.

...He was supposed to be from
Raza. However, records state
that his appearance was
definitely not Human.
His name is only passed down\nas "<font color=yellow>Kevin</font>."

And... the researchers from
Rigas led by that Kevin were
the ones who made the conflict
between the Raza and Ober
permanent.
...I see. So the people of Rigas\njust went ahead and made the\nStardust Bazaar independent.
I see. This satellite is roughly\nthe same size as a normal\nrocky planet.

If the population rooted here
moved as a whole, along with
the Gem mining technology,
independence would be
possible.
But why do that all of a\nsudden?
It's obvious that doing that\nwould cause problems for both\nRaza and Ober.

Normally, wouldn't Raza and
Ober have teamed up to stop
the independence and turned
against the Bazaar?
Monopoly.
Huh?
If that story is true, it means\nthe Bazaar ended up with a\nmonopoly on Gems.
They had their throats held by\nthe energy supply. There was\nno way they could fight back.

In other words, no one is
stupid enough to pick a fight
while saying, "Give me your
fuel."
...That makes sense.
I don't understand why Kevin\nforced independence.
But it's a fact that a great\nmany people followed Kevin.

As a result, a three-way
deadlock was established
between Raza, Ober, and the
Bazaar...
...But.

That's when, twenty years ago,
the issue of ownership over
the planet Lazuli suddenly
cropped up.

Planet Lazuli is a world of sand
and wasteland. It has no
underground resources, no
plants, and no water.
Only the atmosphere was of a\ntype compatible with the Raza\nand most Ober,

but it was judged to be entirely
unsuitable for habitation, so it
was ignored from the early
days of space development.
What? There's an atmosphere\nthe Raza can breathe, but no\nwater?

That's right. I passed by it
once on a mission, and it's a
lonely planet of nothing but
reddish-brown.
...I see. That's strange.
The Bazaar didn't pay any\nattention to Lazuli either.

It's too far to be a relay point
for starships, and there are no
useful planets or resources
nearby.

So, in truth... the Bazaar
doesn't actually understand
why the Raza and Ober are
fighting over Lazuli.
Huh? Are you serious?

Dead serious. To be honest,
even as a former member of
the Raza army, I was never
told a clear reason.

Officially, within the Raza army,
the story is that it's to secure
a bridgehead for outer space
development and to search for
new Gem veins... but that's
about it.

Even the Ober refugees who
came to the Bazaar didn't
seem to know why Planet
Lazuli was necessary.

You've gotta be kidding. You're
telling me they've been fighting
for nearly 20 years without
even knowing what they're
fighting for?
Yep. The cost-performance is\nabsolute garbage.

Honestly, I think it would be far
more economical to just
humble themselves before the
Bazaar and buy Gems.
People actually feel that way.\nEven within Raza's army, war\nweariness is starting to set in.

Regardless of the reason, once
you've kept it up for 20 years,
you can't just stop even if the
original problem is solved.
Not after they've spent all this\ntime killing each other.
...Yeah, that's pretty much it.
Hmm. In the end, we still don't\nknow what Raza and Ober\nactually want from Lazuli...

But I finally understand why
the Bazaar can afford to just
stand by and watch while the
two fight so fiercely.
And why Lavarnia's father\ncalled it a pathetic little planet.

But even if it's that kind of
planet, there must be some
reason why Raza and Ober
have spent 20 years fighting
over it.
*Sigh*... I just hope we don't\nend up having to visit Planet\nLazuli at some point...

Captain, we've arrived at the
point where the smuggler's
ship was sunk.	machine
6022_070_27	6950007d7622f8ea2100a42159d10f16fb3521c0	...Unfortunately, there appear
to be no survivors. I need
everyone to come to the
Bridge.
Understood. That's enough\ntalk, let's go.
...Karlyn.
What?
How many more years do you\nhave left to live?
Huh? Where is this coming\nfrom all of a sudden?
The Holy War is finally over,\nbut then again, in the future...

I just thought it would suck if
something like this happened in
the future Daftine, where Tika
and the others are born.
...200 years from now, huh? It's\nactually quite possible, which is\nthe problem.
Don't call it a problem.
Still, I'll leave everything to the\nothers once you've reached\nthe end of your lifespan.

Until then, you'd better do your
best. Though, I suspect you
wouldn't even die if someone
killed you.
What exactly do you think I\nam...
This thing... Just what on earth\nwould have to happen for it to\nbe broken like this?
It's been completely snapped in\ntwo.

I scanned the fracture point. I
have determined that these
are signs of a tear caused by
the impact of a collision with a
massive object, not heat.
So, you're saying it was an\naccident?
I can't rule out that possibility.\nHowever, there is one strange\nthing.

A large amount of a specific
substance was floating only
around the wreckage. It was a
component not found in the
surrounding rocks or debris.
I'm running an analysis on it\nnow.

Administrator Koro is pushing
the Overman's component
analysis capabilities to the limit
to investigate the substance in
question.

It will take some time as data
must be exchanged with AI
Rekoro, but I expect it to be
completed in about half a day.

No, we're leaving the wreckage
here. If it was a proper ship,
the black box should continue
to emit a signal for a certain
period.
All we can do is pray that\nOber's people pick it up.

...It can't be helped. The
Overman is a pirate ship, and
the other party were
smugglers.

Both sides know that in the
event of an accident, they're
prepared to become space
dust.
One wrong move and we could\nhave ended up just like them...

...It may seem heartless, but
we'll recover those Gems. If
they can't take them back, we
might as well put them to use.

Actually, about that―I've been
scanning the area, but I can't
find the container that held the
Gems anywhere.
...What?
The impact of the sinking may\nhave sent it flying far away.
Unless the container has a\ntransmitter, searching for it will\nbe impossible.
...What a waste.
Talk about being ruthless.

It can't be helped. We have to
move to the next point. For the
sake of not letting their
sacrifice be in vain, we'll
proceed with caution.
So this is a sample of\nwhatever crushed that\nsmuggler's ship.
I can't say for certain, though.

It's much more brittle than the
surrounding rock, so unless it
hits something at an incredibly
high speed, I doubt a clump of
this would cause much of an
impact.
I see... it certainly crumbles\nquite easily.
I wonder if I should have made\nsome hardware modifications\nto the Overman...

If you treat it as if it's the
same as a GFSS-3214F, you
end up with all sorts of
delays...

I don't know how much longer
this composition analysis will
take. Verda, could you give me
a hand?
I don't mind. Let's see... this is\nindeed a primitive composition\nscanner...
Isn't this a silicon-based\nsubstance?
Hmm?
What? Silicon?
Look at this section. It's\nidentical to the silicic acid\nformed inside plants.
Can you tell just by looking at\nit?
On Ex Giva, we had to regularly\nimprove the grain-based foods\nwe grew.
Silicon is essential for a plant's\namount of photosynthesis and\nfor reducing stress,

so I had to adjust it quite
precisely to match the changes
in the plants themselves and
the traits of the races
consuming them.

Start your identification from
the silicon-based molecular
structure. It is likely a closely
related substance.
Understood. I'll give it a try.
...Still, though.
Hmm?

How is it that you can do such
calm analysis, but then you act
like that whenever you're in
front of Eve's or Karlyn's
crests?

It is the difference between
the known and the unknown.
When people try to move
forward by their own power,
they often struggle
pathetically.
I feel like it's not even on that\nlevel...

If you are too rude to me, your
"points" will start piling up, and
you'll be in for a treat when we
return to our ship.

Ah, that mysterious point
system... it brings back
memories! I'm going back to the
analysis!!
Running away is futile...

But even if it is a silicon-based
substance, I wonder why
something like that was
floating.

So the next point is the last
one. I'm glad there haven't
been any major troubles since
the first incident...
To think the final hand-off is on\nan asteroid near Planet Lazuli.
Is it really safe to trade so\nclose to such a heavy combat\nzone?

...The hand-off point itself is
fine, as I made sure it was
specified far from the
battlefield.

Besides, the next contact isn't
some low-rent smuggler like
the others. The reward is
exceptional for that reason.
Which is why I'm being\nselective about who goes for\nthis next trade.
Is it not enough to have me,\nEuwin, Welch, and Karlyn like\nbefore?
...You stay hidden this time.\nAnd if possible, the Captain\nand Ricardo too.
And why is that?
The next contact is the Raza\nSpace Force 5th Fleet.

You and Ricardo look like
soldiers at a glance, so it
would be a bit troublesome if
you were spotted.
The 5th Fleet!? You're dealing\ndirectly with the military! Aren't\nwe going to get seized!
...That won't happen. We've\nbeen doing business with the\n5th Fleet for nearly ten years.
No, but... what if something like\nthat time happens again...?
...I can't believe you have the\nnerve to say that.
Ah, well...
...I've looked into that woman's\naffiliation.
The 1st Fleet. She was a\nsupervisor for the front-line\nunits.
You could call it my father's\nmistake, I suppose...
Since then, both Raza and\nOber have only dealt with\npartners they can truly trust.
It's made things tighter\nfinancially, but you can't put a\nprice on safety.
I-I see.
So, even if you return to that\nwoman, please don't report the\n5th Fleet's illegal trades.
The money from the 5th Fleet\nis what keeps the refugees at\nthe Bazaar alive.
It may be illegal, but it's a\nreality we can't change. Please\ndon't forget that.
...I get it. I know the boss's\n"purity" isn't that kind of thing.
I wonder.
So, you're taking Heath out\nand just want the three of us?

...Truthfully, it would be
reassuring to have you,
Karlyn... but we need to carry
cargo onto their ship.
They likely won't let Karlyn of\nFoxtail inside.
That's why I want to ask Euwin,\nWelch, and Tika.
